referenceSources.description:
The 1989 Ferrari F40 LM, codenamed F40 Corsa, represents a track-focused evolution of the iconic F40 supercar. Finished on June 20, 1988, its 2936 cm³ engine block was reworked for improved cooling and paired with Marelli‑Weber electronics, IHI turbochargers, and larger Secan intercoolers. Composite chassis elements increased rigidity by 65%, while 355 mm Brembo ventilated discs and 4‑piston calipers provided race‑grade braking performance. Aerodynamic upgrades include a concave venturi front undertray and an adjustable dual‑element rear wing.

Testing began on October 25, 1988, at Ferrari’s Fiorano circuit, where Dario Benuzzi recorded a 1’23”01 lap time. Over 23 sessions at Fiorano, Monza, Paul Ricard, Jarama, Lédenon, and Vallelunga, the F40 LM reached 367 km/h at Nardò. Drivers such as Jean‑Pierre Jabouille, Michel Ferté, and Jean Alesi contributed to its development. Initially intended for the European GTC championship, the car was adapted for IMSA competition with intake restrictors and added ballast to comply with regulations.
